en: A text added to the end of a book or an article, containing additional information.
The vermiform appendix.

ex.en: The surgeon took out his patient's appendix.
ex.ja: 外科医は患者の盲腸を摘出した。

note.ja: ラテン語 appendix（付け足し）から。ad + pendere（ぶら下げる）。「付録」→ 腸にぶら下がる部分 →「虫垂」。append と同じ。

en: A large room for public meetings or performances.
The space where the audience is located in a theater, etc.

auditorium.ety: Borrowed from Latin audītōrium, from audītōrius (“pertaining to hearing”). Equivalent to auditory + -ium.

ex.en: This auditorium can seat up to 300 people.
ex.ja: この講堂は300人まで入れる。

ex.en: The crowd poured out of the auditorium.
ex.ja: 群集は公会堂からどっと出てきた。

ex.en: The auditorium is filled to capacity with anxious applicants.
ex.ja: 講堂は熱心な応募者でいっぱいだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 auditorium（聞く場所）から。audire（聞く）。「講堂」。audio と同じ aud。

en: Kind; gentle; mild.
Of a climate or environment, mild and favorable.

benign.ety: From Middle English benigne, benygne, from Old French benigne, from Latin benignus (“kind, good”), from bene (“well”) + genus (“origin, kind”). Compare malign.

ex.en: The tumor was benign.
ex.ja: 腫瘍は良性でした。

note.ja: ラテン語 benignus（親切な）から。bene（よく）+ gignere（生まれる）。「生まれのよい」→「優しい・良性の」。malignant（悪性の）の対。benefit と同じ bene。

en: A chemical, such as sodium hypochlorite or hydrogen peroxide, or a preparation of such a chemical, used for disinfecting or whitening.
A variety of bleach.
To treat with bleach, especially so as to whiten (fabric, paper, etc.) or lighten (hair).
To be whitened or lightened (by the sun, for example).

bleach.ety:
From Middle English blechen, from Old English blǣċan (“to bleach, whiten”), from Proto-West Germanic *blaikijan, from Proto-Germanic *blaikijaną, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰel- (“to shine”).
Cognate with Dutch bleken (“to bleach”), German bleichen (“to bleach”), Danish blege, Swedish bleka (“to bleach”). Related to Old English blāc (“pale”) (English blake; compare also bleak).

ex.en: I need to get my hair bleached at the salon.
ex.ja: サロンで髪を脱色してもらわないとな。

note.ja: 古英語 blǣcan（白くする）から。bleak（白っぽい・荒涼とした）と同系。

en: An alcoholic liquor distilled from wine or fermented fruit juice.
Any variety of such liquor.
To preserve, flavour, or mix with brandy.

brandy.ety: Shortened form of brandywine, from Dutch brandewijn (“burnt wine”). Compare German Brantewein, Branntwein, Danish brændevin.

ex.en: The brandy brought him around in no time.
ex.ja: ブランデーですぐに意識を回復した。

ex.en: Put a little of brandy in my tea.
ex.ja: 紅茶にブランデーを少し入れてください。

ex.en: The brandy is getting to my head.
ex.ja: ブランデーがまわってきたぞ。

note.ja: オランダ語 brandewijn（焼いたワイン）から。蒸留したワイン。burn と同系。

ja: 瀬戸際（on the brink of：今にも〜しそうで）

en: The edge, margin, or border of a steep place, as of a precipice; a bank or edge.
The edge or border.

brink.ety: From Middle English brinke, brenke, from Old Norse *brenka, brekka, from Proto-Germanic *brinkǭ, *brinkaz (“hill, edge (of land)”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰren- (“to project”). Cognate with Dutch brink (“grassland”), regional German Brink, Icelandic brekka (“slope”); also Tocharian B prenke (“island”), Irish braine (“prow”).

ex.en: The man was on the brink of death.
ex.ja: その男は死にかけていた。

ex.en: The world is on the brink of destruction.
ex.ja: 世界は破滅の淵に立たされている。

ex.en: We stood on the brink of a cliff.
ex.ja: 私たちはがけのふちに立った。

note.ja: 北欧語に由来するとされる。「縁」→「瀬戸際」。

en: A carved object.
The act or craft of producing a carved object.
Executing turns without pivoting.

ex.en: This carving knife ... it's one made by a famous swordsmith.
ex.ja: この包丁・・・有名な刀匠が作ったものなんです。

ex.en: In that exhibition you will see jade carvings by several famous masters.
ex.ja: その展覧会では、複数の有名な巨匠のヒスイの彫刻が見られるでしょう。

ex.en: "What's this?" "It's called a 'chisel', it's a tool used for carving wood."
ex.ja: 「これ何？」「これは木を彫る道具で『彫刻刀』っていうんだよ」

note.ja: carve（彫る）+ -ing。「彫刻」。

en: Impudent; impertinent; impertinently bold, often in a way that is regarded as endearing or amusing.
Tending to expose the cheeks of the buttocks.

cheeky.ety:
From cheek + -y.
Compare typologically barefaced, bald-faced; Italian sfacciato (< Latin ex- + faciēs); French effronté, Italian sfrontato (< Latin ex- + frons), Polish czelny (< czoło).

ex.en: Don't be so cheeky.
ex.ja: 生意気を言うんじゃない。

note.ja: cheek（ほお・生意気）+ -y。「生意気な」。

ex.ja: 私の友人には２人の研究者がいる。一人は言語学者で、もう一人は化学者だ。

note.ja: alchemist（錬金術師）の短縮。「化学者」→（英）「薬剤師」。

ex.ja: 海が海岸に入り込んだ。

note.ja: coast（海岸）+ line（線）。「海岸線」。

en: Any of the genus Naja of venomous snakes that can spread their neck ribs into a broad hood when threatened; a true cobra.
A ring-necked spitting cobra or rinkhals (Hemachatus haemachatus).

cobra.ety: Borrowed from Portuguese cobra, from Latin colubra (“a female snake”).

note.ja: ポルトガル語 cobra de capello（ずきんをかぶったヘビ）の短縮。

en: To work together with others to achieve a common goal.
To voluntarily cooperate treasonably, as with an enemy occupation force in one's country.

collaborate.ety: Back-formation from collaborator, from French collaborateur, or else modeled on French collaborer or directly from Late Latin collabōrātus, past participle of collabōrāre. Displaced native Old English efnwyrċan.

note.ja: col（共に）+ labor（働く）+ ate。共に働く →「協力する・共同制作する」。

en: In a comparative manner.
When compared to other entities.

comparatively.ety:

ex.en: American senior citizens are comparatively well-off.
ex.ja: アメリカのお年寄りは比較的裕福である。

ex.en: The prices of Japanese automobiles are still comparatively high.
ex.ja: 日本車の価格は、比較的高い。

ex.en: There's a comparatively large cinema complex inside the mall.
ex.ja: モールの中に、比較的大きなシネコンがある。

note.ja: comparative（比較の）+ -ly。「比較的」。compare はラテン語 comparare（並べる）、com + par（等しい）。

en: The universe regarded as a system with harmony and order.
A harmonious, ordered whole.

cosmos.ety:
From Middle English cossmos (“the universe; the world”), borrowed from Ancient Greek κόσμος (kósmos, “order; universe; the earth, the world; decoration, ornament”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱens- (“to announce, proclaim; to put in order”).
The plural form cosmoi is a learned borrowing from Ancient Greek κόσμοι (kósmoi).

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kosmos（秩序・世界）から。「宇宙」。花のコスモスは整った花びらから。cosmetic と同じ。

en: The end of a shirt sleeve that covers the wrist.
The end of a pants leg when folded up.
To furnish with cuffs.

cuff.ety: From Middle English cuffe, coffe (“glove, mitten”), of obscure origin. Perhaps from Old English cuffie (“hood, cap”), from Medieval Latin cofia, cofea, cuffa, cuphia (“helmet, headdress, hood, cap”), from Frankish *kuf(f)ja (“headdress”), from Proto-West Germanic *kuppju, from Proto-Germanic *kupjō (“cap”). Cognate with Middle High German kupfe (“cap”).

ex.en: I'm not good at speaking off the cuff.
ex.ja: 私は即興で話すのが苦手だ。

ex.en: He made a splendid off-the-cuff speech.
ex.ja: 彼は即席に立派な演説をした。

note.ja: 中英語 cuffe（手袋）から。「袖口」→ 手首にはめる →「手錠（cuffs）」。

A tropical cyclone occurring in the South Pacific or Indian Ocean.
To separate using a cyclone separator.
To storm as a cyclone.

A person suffering from a delusion.

en: The removal of someone from office.
The act of depositing material, especially by a natural process; the resultant deposit.

deposition.ety: From Middle English deposicion, from Old French deposicion (French déposition), from Latin depositio.

note.ja: de（下に）+ pos（置く）+ ition。下に置くこと →「堆積・（法廷外の）宣誓証言・退位」。

en: Steady application; industry; careful work involving long-term effort.
The qualities of a hard worker, including conscientiousness, determination, and perseverance.

diligence.ety: Borrowed from French diligence, from Latin diligentia.

ex.en: This book should be read with diligence.
ex.ja: この本は丹念に読まなければならない。

ex.en: Diligence is essential to success in life.
ex.ja: 勤勉は人生の成功に不可欠である。

ex.en: Her diligence is a good example to us all.
ex.ja: 彼女の勤勉さは良い見本だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 diligere（大切にする・選ぶ）から。di + legere（選ぶ）。「勤勉」。elect と同じ leg。

en: To make distinctions.
To treat or affect differently, depending on differences in traits.
Having its differences marked; distinguished by certain tokens.

discriminate.ety: First attested in 1615; borrowed from Latin discrīminātus, perfect passive participle of discrīminō (“to divide, separate, distinguish”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (adjective-forming suffix)), from discrīmen (“a space between, division, separation, distinction”), from discernō (“to divide, separate, distinguish, discern”). By surface analysis, dis- + criminate.

ex.en: You should not discriminate against people because of their sex.
ex.ja: 性別で人を分け隔てすべきでない。

ex.en: We must be able to discriminate between objects and situations.
ex.ja: 我々は物事と状況を区別する事ができないといけない。

ex.en: Subtle differences in tone discriminate the original from the copy.
ex.ja: 原画と複製とでは色調に微妙な差異がある。

note.ja: ラテン語 discrimen（区別）から。dis（離れて）+ cri（ふるい分ける）。ふるい分けて区別する →「区別する・差別する」。

en: A tactic used to draw attention away from the real threat or action.
A hobby; an activity that distracts the mind.

diversion.ety: From Middle English diversion, dyversioun, from Medieval Latin diversiō, from Latin divertō (“to divert”); see divert.

note.ja: di（離れて）+ vers（向ける）+ ion。別の方へ向けること →「迂回・気晴らし・流用」。

en: The passage of a door; a door-shaped entrance into a house or a room.
An opening or passage in general.

ex.en: Her sudden appearance in the doorway surprised us.
ex.ja: 彼女が突然玄関に姿を見せたので我々はびっくりした。

ex.en: A man suddenly appeared in the doorway.
ex.ja: 突然人が玄関に現れた。

ex.en: There's someone at the doorway.
ex.ja: だれか玄関にいる。

note.ja: door（戸）+ way（通路）。「戸口」。

en: A large, usually metal trash receptacle designed to be hoisted up by a garbage truck in order to be emptied.

dumpster.ety: Genericized brand name, from blend of dump + Dempster. The original brand (and some associated things) are no longer trademarked, because the three trademarks involved have either expired or been cancelled. By surface analysis, dump + -ster.

note.ja: Dempster Dumpster（商標）から。dump（捨てる）+ -ster。

To select or copy sample material (excerpts) from a work.

False in the sense of made-up, constructed.

en: An enemy.

A native or resident of the state of Georgia in the United States of America.

Of, from, or pertaining to the U.S. state of Georgia or its Georgian English dialect.

en: A means of escape.
The effecting of an escape.
Pertaining to an escape, as in a vehicle or plans.

note.ja: get away（逃げる）の名詞化。「逃走・短い休暇」。

en: Originally, enchantment; magic charm; especially, the effect of a spell that causes one to see objects in a form that differs from realit…
Alluring beauty or charm (often with sex appeal).
To enchant; to bewitch.

Borrowed from Scots glamour (“magic”), alteration of Middle English gramere (“grammar”), from Old French gramaire. Doublet of glamoury, gramarye, grammar, and grimoire.

ex.en: She's a glamor girl.
ex.ja: 彼女はグラマーだね。

note.ja: grammar（学問）のスコットランドでの変化形とされる。学問が魔術と見なされたことから「魔法 → 魅力」。

en: A container in which papers to be dealt with are put.
An electronic folder serving the same purpose, but for electronic files, especially email.
To put (something) in someone's inbox.
To communicate with (a person) by writing to their electronic inbox.

ex.en: My inbox is full.
ex.ja: 受信トレイがいっぱいだ。

ex.en: Emails have started suddenly disappearing from my inbox.
ex.ja: 受信トレイからメールが突然消えはじめた。

Not of central or critical importance.

ex.ja: ちなみに、言わなくちゃいけないことがあるんだ。

ex.en: The film we incidentally watched yesterday was well worth watching.
ex.ja: 昨日、たまたま見た動画は、とても為になる話だった。

note.ja: incidental（付随的な）+ -ly。incident（出来事）、in + cadere（落ちる）。「ついでながら」。

en: In an infinite manner; as of anything growing without bounds; endlessly.
To a surpassingly large extent.

ex.ja: 多くの天文学者は、宇宙は永遠に膨張してゆくものだと考えている。

note.ja: infinite + -ly。「無限に・はるかに」。

en: Filled with air or fluid
Expanded; in a state of inflation, of abnormally increased size, amount, etc.

ex.en: When I drink carbonated water my stomach quickly starts feeling inflated.
ex.ja: 炭酸を飲むとすぐにお腹が膨れる。

ex.en: The frog inflated himself more and more, until finally he burst.
ex.ja: カエルはどんどん腹をふくらませとうとう破裂してしまった。

Intermediate between extremes.

mediate.ety: The adjective is first attested in the 1440s in Middle English, the verb in 1538; from Middle English mediat(e) (“intermediate; intercessory”), borrowed from Late Latin mediātus, perfect passive participle of mediō (“to divide in the middle; (in Medieval Latin) to be in the middle, be or become between, mediate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (adjective-forming suffix)), from medius (“middle”) + -ō (verb-forming suffix).

ex.en: He mediated between the two parties.
ex.ja: 彼は両当事者の間を調停した。

ex.en: The Norwegian diplomat mediated the secret negotiations that produced the historic document.
ex.ja: ノルウェー人外交官が、歴史的文書を生んだ秘密交渉を取り持った。

note.ja: medi（中間）+ ate。間に立つ →「仲裁する・調停する」。

en: Negotiation to resolve differences conducted by an impartial party.
The act of intervening for the purpose of bringing about a settlement.

ex.ja: 彼女の仲裁が私たちの口論を終わらせた。

note.ja: medi（中間）+ ation。間に立つこと →「調停・仲裁」。

en: Thousand-year-old; also (by extension, loosely) thousands of years old.

millennial.ety:
The adjective is a learned borrowing from Late Latin mīllennium (“millennium”) + English -al (suffix meaning ‘of or pertaining to’ forming adjectives; and forming nouns). The English word may be analysed as millennium + -al or milli- (prefix meaning ‘thousand’) + -ennial (suffix meaning ‘years’).
Adjective sense 5 (“of or relating to, or characteristic of, people born in the last two decades of the 20th century”) was coined by the American authors William Strauss (1947–2007) and Neil Howe (born 1951) in their book Generations (1991): see the quotations.
The noun is derived from the adjective.

note.ja: millennium（千年）+ -al。2000年前後に成人した「ミレニアル世代」。

Promoting moral and mental well-being.

en: A person, especially an artist or writer, who lives an unconventional or nonconformist lifestyle.

bohemian.ety:
Borrowed from French bohémien (“person from Bohemia”), from Bohême (“Bohemia”), equivalent to Bohemia + -an.

The term bohémien was then adopted to describe members of the scene of artists and intellectuals who lived unconventional and impoverished lifestyles in Paris, perceived as living like gypsies. Popularized by the 1851 Henri Murger novel Scenes of Bohemian Life (Scènes de la vie de bohème).

ex.ja: ゆりかごの中の赤ん坊はとてもかわいい。

note.ja: 古英語 cradol（揺りかご）から。「揺りかご」→ 文明の揺りかご →「発祥地」。

en: Having any difficulty or impediment which can be likened to a crippling injury.

ex.en: The Tokaido Line was crippled by the typhoon.
ex.ja: 東海道線は台風で麻痺状態になった。

ex.en: Old and crippled, he had courage enough to do the work.
ex.ja: 年をとり、身体も不自由であったが、彼にはその仕事をする気力があった。

note.ja: cripple（不自由にする）+ -ed。古英語 crypel（はう人）。「機能しなくなった」。人に使うと差別的に響く。

en: The quality of being decent; propriety.
That which is proper or becoming.

decency.ety: From Latin decentia, from decens. Equivalent to decent + -cy. Compare French décence.

ex.en: He didn't have the decency to admit that he was wrong.
ex.ja: 彼には自分が悪かったことを認めるぐらいの心得もなかった。

ex.en: She had the decency to apologize.
ex.ja: 謝るぐらいの礼儀は彼女も心得ていた。

ex.en: That is beneath ordinary decency.
ex.ja: そんなことをするのは礼儀の常識を欠いている。

note.ja: decent（きちんとした）+ -cy。ラテン語 decere（ふさわしい）。「礼儀正しさ・良識」。

en: To regard with contempt or scorn.
To disregard or ignore.

despise.ety: From Middle English despisen, from Old French despis-, stem of despire, from Latin dēspicere (“to look down upon, despise, scorn”), from dē (“down”) + speciō (“to look at”). Displaced native Old English forsēon.

ex.en: She despises him only because he is poor.
ex.ja: 彼が貧しいというだけの理由で彼女は彼を軽蔑している。

ex.en: He despises people of a lower social class.
ex.ja: 彼は社会的地位の低い人を軽蔑する。

ex.en: Don't despise a man because he is poor.
ex.ja: 貧しいからといって人を軽蔑してはならない。

note.ja: de（下へ）+ spis（見る）+ e。見下ろす →「軽蔑する」。

en: That which destroys something.
A small, fast warship with light gun armament, smaller than a cruiser, but bigger than a frigate.

destroyer.ety: Inherited from Middle English destroyour, destroyere; By surface analysis, destroy + -er. Designating a warship, it is ellipsis of torpedo-boat destroyer, the longer term appearing at the end of the 19th century and the shorter form early in the 20th.

note.ja: destroy（破壊する）+ -er。de + struere（積む）。「積んだものを崩す人」→「破壊者・駆逐艦」。

en: An administrative division of the later Roman Empire, established by the Herodian tetrarchy.
An ecclesiastical territory administered by a bishop.

diocese.ety: From Middle English diocise, from Old French diocese, from Late Latin diocēsis, from Latin dioecēsis (“district under a governor”), from Ancient Greek διοίκησις (dioíkēsis, “internal administration”).

note.ja: ギリシャ語 dioikēsis（管理・行政区）から。dia + oikein（住む）。「司教区」。

en: Spread out in space and/or time; not concentrated.

ex.en: The rising sun dispersed the mist.
ex.ja: 朝日が霧をおいやった。

ex.en: The bank robbers dispersed in all directions.
ex.ja: 銀行強盗たちは四方八方に散らばった。

note.ja: disperse（散らす）+ -ed。「散らばった」。

en: An outside step leading up to the door of a building, usually a home.
One's immediate neighborhood or locality.
To visit one household after another to solicit sales, charitable donations, political support, etc.
To corner somebody for an unexpected interview.

ex.en: The newspaper is delivered to my doorstep every morning by the local delivery boy.
ex.ja: 新聞は毎朝、地元の配達の子が玄関先まで届けてくれます。

note.ja: door（戸）+ step（踏み段）。「玄関先」。

en: To go aboard a craft or vessel for transportation.
To start, begin.

embark.ety: Borrowed from Middle French embarquer, from em- + barque (“small ship”). Compare with Portuguese embarcar, Spanish abarcar.

ex.en: They embarked on the new project full of hope.
ex.ja: 彼らは希望に胸をふくらませてその新しい事業に乗り出した。

ex.en: The old couple embarked on a tour around the world.
ex.ja: その老夫婦は世界一周旅行に出かけた。

ex.en: He embarked on a new enterprise.
ex.ja: 彼は新しい事業に乗り出した。

note.ja: em（中に）+ barca（小舟）。「船に乗り込む」→「着手する」。barge と同じ。

en: To enhance.
To make (someone or something) rich or richer.

enrich.ety: From Middle English enrichen, from Anglo-Norman enrichir and Old French enrichier. By surface analysis, en- + rich.

ex.en: The discovery of oil enriched the country.
ex.ja: 石油の発見でその国は裕福になった。

ex.en: You should enrich your mind when young.
ex.ja: 若い時に心を豊かにするべきだ。

ex.en: I want to have a full and enriching student-life.
ex.ja: 大いに充実した学生生活を送りたい。

note.ja: en（〜にする）+ rich（豊かな）。「豊かにする」。

en: To supply with something necessary in order to carry out a specific action or task; to provide with (e.g. weapons, provisions, munitions,…
To dress up; to array; to clothe.

equip.ety:
From French équiper (“to supply, fit out”), originally said of a ship, Old French esquiper (“to embark”); of Germanic origin, most probably from Old Norse skipa (“to man (a ship)”), from Proto-Germanic *skipōną (“to ship, sail, embark”).
Compare with Middle High German schipfen, German schiffern, Icelandic skipa, Old English scipian. Doublet of ship.

ex.en: He wants to equip his son with a good education.
ex.ja: 彼は息子に十分な教育を身につけさせたいと思っている。

note.ja: 古フランス語 equiper（船を艤装する）から。北欧語 skipa（船を整える）、ship と同じ。「備え付ける」。

en: Used as a general intensifier; a pfella.

note.ja: fellow のくだけた発音。「やつ・男」。

Appealing, enticing.

Something that grows.

en: One who handles something (especially manually) or someone.
A controller, trainer, someone who handles a specified thing, animal or person (especially a prizefighter).

handler.ety: From Middle English handler, handiller, equivalent to handle + -er.

note.ja: handle（扱う）+ -er。「扱う人・調教師」。

en: Negative effects, such as headache or nausea, caused by previous drunkenness due to (excessive) consumption of alcohol.
Similar negative effects caused by previous excessive consumption of another substance, such as a drug, coffee, sugar, etc.

hangover.ety: American English; hang + over. First sense was first attested in 1904. Third sense was first attested in 1894.

ex.en: This morning was tough because of my hangover.
ex.ja: 今朝は二日酔いで辛かったです。

ex.en: On the following day, we all had terrible hangovers.
ex.ja: 次の朝はみんなひどい二日酔いでした。

ex.en: Tom went to work with a hangover.
ex.ja: トムは二日酔いのまま仕事に行ったんだ。

note.ja: hang over（残る）の名詞化。「前夜の酒が残ったもの」→「二日酔い」。

en: One who hates.

hater.ety: From Middle English hatere, equivalent to hate + -er. Compare Old English hetend, hettend (“enemy”, literally “hater”). Cognate with Dutch hater (“hater”), German Hasser, Hässer (“hater”), Danish hader (“hater”), Swedish hatare (“hater”), Icelandic hatari (“hater”).

ex.en: He is a woman hater.
ex.ja: 彼は女嫌いだ。

note.ja: hate（憎む）+ -er。「嫌う人・アンチ」。

en: Widespread devastation and destruction.
Mayhem.
To pillage.
To cause havoc.
A cry in war as the signal for indiscriminate slaughter.

havoc.ety: From Middle English havok, havyk, from Old French havok in the phrase crier havok (“cry havoc”) a signal to soldiers to seize plunder, from Old French crier (“cry out, shout”) + havot (“pillaging, looting”), of obscure origin. Probably from a derivative of Old French *haf, hef (“hook”), from Frankish *haf, *habbjā, *happjā (“pruning-hook, scythe”), derived from Proto-Germanic *habjaną (“to take up, lift”), related to Old French havee (“handful”), Old French havet (“pruning-hook”), Old High German habba, heppa (“pruning-hook, scythe”), modern German Hippe (“billhook”). If so, then also related

ex.en: His statement raised havoc.
ex.ja: 彼の発言は混乱を引き起こした。

ex.en: An enormous number of insects hatched this year, wreaking havoc on crops.
ex.ja: 今年は、おびただしい数の害虫が発生して、農作物に多大な被害が起きた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 havot（略奪）から。cry havoc（略奪の合図をする）→「大混乱」。

en: Located at the rear (most often said of animals' body parts).
Backward; to the rear.
A doe (female deer), especially a red deer at least two years old.
A spotted food fish of the genus Epinephelus.

Cognate with Gothic 𐌷𐌹𐌽𐌳𐌰𐌽𐌰 (hindana, “from beyond”), Old Norse hindr (“obstacle”), Old Norse handan (“from that side, beyond”), Old High German hintana (“behind”), German hinter (“behind, beyond”), Old English hinder (“behind, back, in the farthest part, down”), Latin

ex.en: The horse rose on its hind legs.
ex.ja: 馬が後ろ足で立った。

ex.en: Devil take the hindmost.
ex.ja: 遅れたやつは鬼に食われろ。

note.ja: 古英語 hindan（後ろから）から。behind と同じ。「後ろの」。

en: One who or that which hits.
One who comes up to bat.

hitter.ety: From hit + -er (agent noun suffix) or -er (measurement suffix).

ex.ja: 彼は目下首位打者だ。

ex.en: He is the leading hitter of the Pacific League at present.
ex.ja: 彼は目下パリーグの首位打者だ。

ex.en: He appeared as a pinch hitter in the game.
ex.ja: 彼はその試合に代打として出場した。

note.ja: hit + -er。「打つ人」。

en: A structure, whether artificial or natural, for housing a swarm of honeybees.
The bees of one hive; a swarm of bees.
To collect (bees) into a hive.
To store (something other than bees) in, or as if in, a hive.

hive.ety:
From Middle English hyve, from Old English hȳf, from Proto-West Germanic *hūfi, from Proto-Indo-European *kuHp- (“water vessel”), from *kew- (“to bend, curve”).
See also Dutch huif (“beehive”), Danish dialect huv (“ship’s hull”); also Latin cūpa (“tub, vat”), Ancient Greek κύπη (kúpē, “gap, hole”), κύπελλον (kúpellon, “beaker”), Sanskrit कूप (kū́pa, “cave”). Doublet of coupe, cup, and keeve.
The computing term was chosen as an in-joke relating to bees; see this for more.

ex.en: I get hives when I eat eggs.
ex.ja: 卵を食べるとじんましんが出ます。

ex.en: He gets hives when he eats eggs.
ex.ja: 卵を食べるとじんましんが出ます。

ex.en: She gets hives when she eats eggs.
ex.ja: 卵を食べるとじんましんが出ます。

note.ja: 古英語 hȳf（ミツバチの巣）から。「巣」→ にぎやかな場所。

Decorated and illustrated.

ex.ja: その部屋は赤い光で照らされていた。

en: To fix firmly or set securely or deeply.
To insert (something) surgically into the body.
Anything surgically implanted in the body, such as a tissue graft or prosthesis, particularly breast implants.
A representative of a travel company, working within the office of a large client and exclusively dealing with that client.

implant.ety: From Middle French implanter, from Latin implantō. By surface analysis, im- + plant.

ex.en: The cochlea implant is a technically ingenious device.
ex.ja: 人工内耳は技術的に巧妙な機器です。

ex.en: Decision to disallow Medicaid for second cochlea implant withdrawn.
ex.ja: ２回目の人工内耳移植への低所得者医療扶助制度の適用不許可を取り下げる。

note.ja: im（中に）+ plantare（植える）。「埋め込む・インプラント」。plant と同じ。

en: To accuse of wrongdoing; charge.
To make a formal accusation or indictment for a crime against (a party) by the findings of a jury, especially a grand jury.

indict.ety:
From Middle English enditen, endyten (“to accuse”), from Old French enditer (“to dictate, indite”), from Late Latin indictāre, frequentative of Latin indicere (“to proclaim”), from in- + dicere (“to say”), or from in- + dictāre (“to say often, to dictate”). Doublet of indite.
The irregular spelling is due to the word having been borrowed into Middle English from Old French, and not from Latin as was the case with most other descendants of dictāre (but see dight). The borrowed /iː/ regularly shifted to /aɪ/ in the course of the Great Vowel Shift; the ⟨c⟩ represents a later attempt at graphic La

ex.en: The company president was indicted for paying kickbacks.
ex.ja: 社長はリベートを支払った件で告発されました。

ex.en: The district attorney indicted him for theft and murder.
ex.ja: 地方検事は彼を盗みと殺人罪で起訴した。

ex.en: In the absence of sufficient proof, the police could not indict him.
ex.ja: 十分な証拠が無くて警察は彼を起訴できなかった。

note.ja: in（〜へ）+ dict（言う）。罪を言い渡す →「起訴する」。発音は［ɪnˈdaɪt］。

Inflamed and painful.

ex.ja: 彼の退屈な話にはいらいらする。

ex.ja: 私は君のことにいらいらせざるを得なかった。

note.ja: irritate（いらいらさせる）+ -ed。ラテン語 irritare（刺激する）。

en: A member of the Macropodidae family of large marsupials with strong hind legs for hopping, native to Australia and New Guinea.
A hooded jacket with a front pocket, usually of fleece material, a kangaroo jacket.
To practice kangaroo care on an infant; to hold a premature infant against the skin.
To hunt kangaroo.
Of or relating to Australia.
Characterized by rapidly jumping prices in securities markets or by belief that the prices are unstable in contrast to bear and bull mark…

kangaroo.ety: Borrowed from Guugu Yimidhirr gangurru (“eastern grey kangaroo”). Despite a popular misconception, the Guugu Yimidhirr term does not mean "I don't know".

ex.en: I was tried in a kangaroo court.
ex.ja: 私は吊し上げを食った。

ex.en: Have you ever seen a kangaroo?
ex.ja: カンガルーを見たことはありますか？

ex.en: Female kangaroos carry their young in their pouches.
ex.ja: カンガルーの雌は子供を腹の袋に入れて動く。

note.ja: オーストラリア先住民の言葉 gangurru から。

en: In the manner of one who knows.
With knowledge of all relevant facts.

knowingly.ety: From Middle English knawyngly, knowyngly. By surface analysis, knowing + -ly.

note.ja: knowing（知っている）+ -ly。「故意に・心得顔で」。
